llm.summary: This is mostly a Chinese mental-model reference skill, but its install instructions can point users to a different package and its scope/financial guidance need review.

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown and JSON only, with no executable files, no hidden network payloads, and no evidence of credential collection or data exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: INSTALL.md instructs users to install 'mental-models' while the artifact metadata slug is 'mental-models-cn', creating a concrete risk that users install a different package than the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several triggers are broad ordinary phrases such as analysis and decision questions, increasing accidental activation; investment templates also provide decision thresholds without clear non-advice guardrails.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The progress tracker is a user-editable Markdown template and the update guide includes publish/delete commands for maintainers, but I found no automatic persistence, background worker, privilege escalation, or runtime mutation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a Markdown knowledge base for mental models, strategy, psychology, and investing; that purpose is coherent, but the advertised 108-model scope conflicts with README/SKILL inventories and some referenced helper scripts are not present.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use the canonical slug 'mental-models-cn' rather than the mismatched INSTALL.md command, treat investment outputs as educational frameworks only, and expect a Chinese-language reference skill with broad activation triggers.
llm.findings:
[T08] unexpected: Confirmed: the install command uses a different package identifier than _meta.json, so this is a real installation-scope concern even though it does not prove malicious content in this artifact.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly confirmed: broad triggers are not deceptive, but several are too generic for a skill that should activate when the user clearly wants mental-model selection.
[SQP-2] expected: Investment content is aligned with the advertised purpose, but the templates include concrete buy/position/stop-loss style decision framing without a clear educational-only disclaimer.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-only presentation is consistent with the 'mental-models-cn' name and artifact framing, though an explicit language note would improve disclosure.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the artifact has inconsistent model counts and version claims across SKILL.md, README.md, and _meta.json, which weakens user understanding of what is actually installed.
[AS3] expected: Downgraded: the cited skills/mental-models paths appear in a maintainer update guide for this same skill, not as runtime instructions to enumerate or read unrelated installed skills.
